title: Conditions of the Master Grain Marketing Agreement: Paperwork Standing Behind Each Contract Opened
content:
A member may hold any number of contracts under Grain Marketing Contracts at the same time, across commodities, crop years and programmes, and the cooperative puts no ceiling on how many they carry. What is governed at opening is the paperwork standing behind them.

**1. The agreement.** A signed master grain marketing agreement covering the crop year of the contract is on file for the member before the contract is opened, on every programme whose catalogue marks the marketing agreement as required.

**2. The credit review.** On every programme whose catalogue requires the credit review, the grain desk credit review for that member is recorded as complete before the contract is opened.

**3. Where the facts are read.** Both facts are read off the member's own contract record, against the contract number the application carries. A member's assurance that the agreement was signed at the counter last week is a clue to go looking, never a substitute for the record.

**4. Where either is missing.** The application is still taken and the contract sits in applied standing, and it is simply not countersigned until the paperwork lands. The desk does not refuse to write the contract and does not backdate it once the paperwork arrives.

**5. Quantity is governed elsewhere.** Quantity, as opposed to count, is governed separately by the open position rule, so a member at their bushel ceiling may still open a further contract for a different crop year.

## The conditions as a table

| Fact | Whose word settles it | When it must stand | Which contract it is read against |
|---|---|---|---|
| Master marketing agreement on file for the crop year | the contract record, not the member | before the contract is opened | the contract number the application carries |
| Grain desk credit review recorded complete | the contract record, not the member | before the contract is opened | the contract number the application carries |

## Points of judgement

A member holding four live contracts across two crop years is not near any limit of count, because there is none. A member whose crop-year agreement is not on the record has their application taken and left in applied standing; the agreement arriving afterwards does not carry the contract back to the day the application was made.
